title.narrative: PIMS 6699 TRAC1 Transforming wildlife conservation and livelihoods at the landscape scale in Mozambique

description.narrative: Mozambique’s globally significant biodiversity is under increasing threat from illegal wildlife trade, habitat loss, and unsustainable land-use practices, compounded by poverty, population pressure, and weak governance. The Gorongosa–Marromeu and Rovuma–Lugenda landscapes are priority ecosystems facing rising deforestation, poaching, and human-wildlife conflict. The objective of the project is to strengthen the integrated management of wildlife conservation and the improvement of livelihoods in these landscapes through transformative approaches, including improved conservation area management, strengthened law enforcement, inclusive land-use planning, and equitable benefit-sharing from wildlife-based economies, with a strong emphasis on empowering women and youth. This transformation will be achieved through four integrated strategies: (1) expanding the effectiveness of conservation area networks and corridor connectivity; (2) strengthening policies, institutions, and technologies to combat illegal wildlife trade; (3) delivering gender-responsive livelihoods and benefit-sharing through challenge grants and mini-grants; and (4) promoting positive community attitudes and behavior change toward biodiversity. As part of the Global Wildlife Program (GWP) under GEF-8, the project is aligned with the program’s goal of addressing key threats to wildlife—illegal trade, human-wildlife conflict, and unsustainable use—while promoting biodiversity conservation and community prosperity. The project is expected to deliver Global Environmental Benefits (GEBs) by reducing poaching and trafficking, restoring ecological corridors, and improving the management of over 3 million hectares of landscapes rich in terrestrial biodiversity, better managing land that serve as wildlife corridors, avoiding CO2 emissions. It will also generate adaptation co-benefits by enhancing ecosystem resilience and communities’ adaptive capacity.

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
